children: HDFC Bank's announcement that Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer Sashidhar Jagdishan will not seek another term has left brokerages broadly positive on the stock but more cautious on its near-term outlook, with several analysts cutting target prices to account for the uncertainty surrounding succession and the bank's strategic direction.

The common thread across brokerage reports is that the leadership transition has introduced a fresh risk premium for India's largest private-sector lender. Yet, after a prolonged period of underperformance and with valuations already compressed, most analysts continue to see enough value in the stock to retain their positive recommendations.
Jefferies retained its Buy rating but cut its price target to Rs 880 from Rs 1,050, while trimming its earnings estimates for FY27-29 by 3% each.

The brokerage said the leadership transition could affect revenue momentum, particularly deposit mobilisation and fee income, while uncertainty could increase the bank's cost of equity and weigh on valuations. Still, it argued that valuations at around 1.5 times one-year forward price-to-book were not demanding enough to warrant a downgrade.

ICICI Securities also retained its Buy rating while cutting its target price to Rs 920 from Rs 1,020. The brokerage reduced its target valuation multiple to around 1.8 times from 2 times earlier to factor in the uncertainty surrounding the MD and CEO succession.

Axis Capital, meanwhile, was more constructive on the immediate impact of Jagdishan's decision. It retained its Buy call with a target price of Rs 1,030, implying significant upside from the price cited in its report. The brokerage said the decision removed concerns surrounding the possibility of a shorter second term and cleared the way for the appointment of a successor with a full three-year tenure.

The difference in tone reflects the market's central dilemma: while Jagdishan's departure has removed one layer of uncertainty about whether he would continue, it has simultaneously opened a much larger question about who will take over and what strategic direction the bank will pursue.
Brokerages see no straightforward succession path.

Jefferies identified Deputy Managing Director Kaizad Bharucha as a possible internal candidate but noted that his remaining tenure could be limited to around 2.8-3 years. It also flagged several possible external candidates, while warning that investors would closely watch for any senior-management exits during the transition.

ICICI Securities similarly said the board had no "easy way forward", noting the limitations associated with both internal and external candidates. An external appointment, it said, could raise risks around cultural integration and senior-management churn, while the new chief executive may also need to undertake difficult strategic changes.
For investors, therefore, the CEO announcement is only the beginning of the next phase.

The bigger question is whether the successor can address the bank's underlying post-merger challenges without sacrificing too much growth. Brokerages continue to point to the funding structure, CASA mobilisation, margins and the return profile as areas requiring attention.
For now, however, valuations appear to be providing a cushion.

Jefferies noted that the stock had already fallen sharply, while ICICI Securities said a significant part of the weakness appeared to be priced in. The extent of any future re-rating, however, is likely to depend less on the mere identity of the next CEO and more on whether the transition is smooth and whether the new leadership can deliver a convincing strategic course correction.

title: HDFC Bank CEO exit: Brokerages retain bullish calls, but slash target prices as succession risks rise
